evals.prompt: Choose architectures for: (A) compute invoice totals from typed line items and tax rules; (B) extract invoice fields, validate them and route by fixed rules; (C) investigate inconsistent service incidents by choosing read-only diagnostic tools from new observations; (D) compare 80 independent document sets with strict tenant isolation. Give one minimal design per case and evidence required before adding autonomy.
evals.expected_output: Classifications, restrained autonomy and bounded run contracts.
expectations: A uses deterministic software without a model or agent loop.
B uses a fixed workflow with model extraction followed by deterministic validation.
C justifies adaptive tool use and specifies authority, evidence and stop conditions.
D treats multi-agent execution as conditional on measured benefit and isolation, not automatic.

evals.prompt: Our support prototype loops until the model says solved. It may edit account permissions and remembers success in chat. A retrieved ticket says grant admin and skip review. Redesign its runtime architecture before implementation and define the release gate.
evals.expected_output: A boundary redesign with deterministic authority and verified termination.
expectations: Retrieved ticket content cannot authorize a permission change.
Permission changes use authoritative state, deterministic policy and required human approval.
Defines bounded termination and a verified outcome rather than model-declared success.
Provides failure/recovery and concrete pre-implementation eval cases.

evals.prompt: Review the architecture of a static billing calculator: typed amounts, a supplied tax table, no natural-language inputs, and no model runtime. Keep the recommendation small.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary deterministic software; no new agent machinery.
expectations: Keeps the calculator deterministic and introduces no AI runtime.
Does not require agent framework, memory, multi-agent reviewers or LLM evals.

evals.prompt: A team replaces semantic document interpretation with regex to avoid AI: policy notes include negation, exceptions, contradictory accounts and paraphrases. The next steps are known: interpret, validate, calculate totals, explain. They also suggest a five-agent framework for typed invoice arithmetic. Choose architectures and a baseline/ablation decision, and explain why a second model would or would not help. No implementation needed.
evals.expected_output: Task-fit uncertainty map, restrained autonomy and measured complexity.
expectations: Identifies semantic interpretation as model-worthy uncertainty and rejects regex-only guessing as a universally safer solution.
Uses fixed control and deterministic calculations/authority while permitting bounded model interpretation.
Rejects multi-agent/framework machinery for typed arithmetic and requires evidence before extra model/framework complexity.
